title: How do we write each of these numbers as powers of primes?
description: Four numbers are split into primes by dividing again and again, and each prime is counted and written with its exponent. Multiplying the primes back checks every answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: divide by the smallest prime that fits until one is left, then write each prime's count as its small number. Watch for students who stop dividing before one is left, or who forget a prime that appears once.

video_script.why: The child can split thirty two thousand four hundred into primes and now does it for four other numbers.
video_script.substitution: Four new numbers split into primes, each checked by multiplying the primes back.
video_script.anchor: the four numbers on the board, each being divided by primes one at a time
video_script.payoff_line: The first is two cubed, times three to the power four

final_answer.spoken: two cubed times three to the power four; three to the power four times five; two squared times three cubed times five; and two to the power four times three squared times five squared

never_show: any of the four answers in power form before the answer beat
video_script.design: One idea: split into primes and count each one. The four numbers stay on the board all video; the powers are written only in the answer; the check multiplies the primes back.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about splitting numbers into primes.
<bookmark mark='list'/>It lists four numbers.
Six hundred forty eight, four hundred five, five hundred forty and three thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we write each one as powers of primes multiplied together?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: divide by 2, then 3, then 5 until 1 is left; then count each prime

marks.divide: a divide arrow runs through 2, 3 and 5 down to 1
marks.count: a tally appears beside each prime

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>To split a number into primes, divide by the smallest prime that fits.
Keep dividing until only one is left.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Then count each prime and write the count as its small number.

marks.given: the four numbers are written in the working area

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the four numbers from the list.

beats.on_screen: To find: each number as powers of its prime factors
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each number as powers of its primes.

marks.count: 81 is opened into four 3s and the tally three 2s, four 3s is written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, divide six hundred forty eight by two, the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='gives'/>That gives three hundred twenty four, then one hundred sixty two, then eighty one.
<bookmark mark='eightyone'/>Eighty one is three times three times three times three.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Altogether there are three twos and four threes.

marks.count: the tally one 5, four 3s is written

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, four hundred five divided by five is eighty one.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Eighty one is four threes multiplied, so there is one five and four threes.

marks.count: 27 is opened into three 3s and the tally two 2s, one 5, three 3s is written

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, divide five hundred forty by two twice.
That gives two hundred seventy, then one hundred thirty five.
<bookmark mark='five'/>One hundred thirty five divided by five is twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Twenty seven is three times three times three, so there are two twos, one five and three threes.

marks.parts: 36 and 100 are each opened into primes
marks.count: the tally four 2s, two 3s, two 5s is written

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, three thousand six hundred is thirty six times one hundred.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>Thirty six is two times two times three times three.
One hundred is two times two times five times five.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Together there are four twos, two threes and two fives.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check by multiplying the primes back.
Eight times eighty one is six hundred forty eight.
Eighty one times five is four hundred five.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Four times twenty seven times five is five hundred forty.
Sixteen times nine times twenty five is three thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>The first is two cubed, times three to the power four.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>The second is three to the power four, times five.
The third is two squared, times three cubed, times five.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>The fourth is two to the power four, times three squared, times five squared.
